text:
Between pain and pleasure stand three creatures,

of whom one looks at a wall,

the second makes use of a sad spirit,

and the third advances on tiptoe;

but, between you and me,

only second creatures exist.


Leaning on my forehead, the day

agrees that, truly,

there is much exactness in space;

but if happiness, which after all has a size,

begins, alas, with my mouth,

who will ask me about my word?


To the instantaneous sense of eternity

there corresponds

this meeting invested with black thread,

but to your temporal farewell

there corresponds only the immutable,

your creature, the soul, my word.

translation.title: Between Pain and Pleasure Stand Three Creatures
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's abstract creatures, exact space, black thread, and word-soul ending.
